previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, and obstructive sleep apnea, was admitted for severe right hip pain lasting nine days. He had recently been hospitalized for left hip effusion and reported frequent infections. Evaluation revealed elevated CRP without signs of systemic infection. Imaging showed mild degenerative changes in the right hip with no effusion or fracture. He was treated with a two-day course of IV methylprednisolone, resulting in significant improvement, and transitioned to a 21-day oral prednisone taper. Facial folliculitis was treated with a seven-day course of Bactrim after initial Unasyn, with clinical improvement. Trace hematuria was noted, requiring outpatient follow-up. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up with rheumatology and primary care for ongoing management.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  US MSK HIP RIGHT

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with right hip pain. Prior hx of the same.  //
Please eval for effusion / abscess

TECHNIQUE:  Limited grayscale and color Doppler images of bilateral hips were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  Right hip radiograph ___

FINDINGS: 

Limited sonographic images of bilateral hips were obtained.  There is a trace
amount of fluid in the right hip joint.  No significant effusion is noted on
the left.  No hypervascularity is detected.

IMPRESSION: 

Trace fluid in the right hip joint.

EXAMINATION:  MRI MSK PELVIS WANDW/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with ankylosing spondylitis, concern for
progression of disease, effusions // sacroiliitis protocol

TECHNIQUE:  Multi sequence and multiplanar imaging of the pelvis was performed
without intravenous contrast on a 1.5 Tesla MRI.

15 mL of intravenous Gadavist was administered.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis from outside hospital ___, right hip
ultrasound ___, right hip radiograph ___, and pelvic radiograph
from outside hospital ___.

FINDINGS: 

No suspicious bone marrow signal. No occult fracture.  There is a small
right-sided hip joint effusion which demonstrates hyperenhancement of the
synovium on postcontrast imaging. There is mild likely reactive bone marrow
edema pattern within the medial acetabulum.  No left-sided hip joint effusion.
No evidence of avascular necrosis.

There is increased fatty marrow in a periarticular distribution along the
bilateral sacroiliac joints, consistent with chronic changes.  No sacroiliac
joint effusion.  In addition, there is mild subchondral bone marrow edema
pattern and enhancement, slightly more prominent on the sacral side at the
inferior aspect of the bilateral sacroiliac joints, suggesting a more active
area of inflammation (series 17, image 22 and 20), worse on the left.

There are bilateral L5 facet joint effusions and possibly also at L3 and L4,
not as well evaluated on this examination.

Visualized pelvic soft tissues are grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

1. Findings consistent with mild bilateral chronic sacroiliitis with small
areas of active inflammation along the inferior joints bilaterally, worse on
the left.

2. Small right hip joint effusion and synovitis with reactive bone marrow
edema pattern in the medial acetabulum.

3. Facet joint effusions at L5, and possibly at L3 and L4 as well, not as well
imaged on this examination.

EXAMINATION:  CT INTERVENTIONAL PROCEDURE

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with ankylosing spondylitis presenting with acute
on chronic SI joint point  // R sacroiliac joint steroid injection

COMPARISON:  MRI pelvis ___ and CT torso from outside hospital ___

PROCEDURE:  CT-guided right sacroiliac joint injection.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ radiologist.
Dr. ___ fellow.

TECHNIQUE:  The risks, benefits, and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient.  After a detailed discussion, informed written
consent was obtained.  A pre-procedure timeout using three patient identifiers
was performed per ___ protocol.

The patient was placed in a prone position on the CT scan table.  Limited
preprocedure CT scan of the intended biopsy area was performed.  Based on the
CT findings, an appropriate position for the right sacroiliac joint injection
was chosen.  The site was marked.

The site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  1% lidocaine
were administered to the subcutaneous and deep tissues for local anesthetic
effect.  Under CT guidance, a 22 gauge spinal needle was introduced into the
right sacroiliac joint and subsequently a combination of 1 cc of Kenalog (40
mg) and 1 cc of 0.25% bupivacaine was instilled into the joint.

The procedure was tolerated well and there were no immediate post-procedural
complications.

DOSE:  DLP:  500 mGy-cm

FINDINGS: 

Mild subchondral sclerosis and narrowing of the sacroiliac joint spaces
bilaterally.  No definite evidence of osseous fusion.  Visualized pelvic soft
tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Mild subchondral sclerosis and joint space narrowing of the bilateral
sacroiliac joints.

2.  Technically successful right sacroiliac joint steroid injection.
